rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template. Its paragraphs 13 and 14 establish substantially the same Tariff Commission machinery later adapted by the child: continuing oversight of trade-agreement concessions, investigations initiated by presidential request or Commission judgment, determination of whether imports cause or threaten serious injury to producers of like or directly competitive articles, public hearings with opportunities to present evidence and be heard, recommendations or reports to the President, and Commission-prescribed procedural rules. C14 contains an earlier, closely related version of that machinery, while C21 applies it in a specific escape-clause proceeding but is less directly a procedural template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whenever in the judgment of the Tariff Commission conditions of competition... have so changed as to warrant it, or upon request of the President, the Commission shall institute a formal investigation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Tariff Commission, upon request of the President, upon its own motion, or upon application of any interested party when in the judgment of the Tariff Commission there is good and sufficient reason therefor, shall make an investigation
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same agency-triggered and President-triggered investigation mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: whether, and, if so, to what extent, the withdrawal, suspension, or modification of a trade-agreement concession remains necessary in order to prevent or remedy serious injury or the threat thereof to the domestic industry concerned
shared_material.parent_excerpt: whether... such article is being imported in such relatively increased quantities and under such conditions as to cause or threaten serious injury to the domestic industry producing like or directly competitive articles... [and recommend] the withdrawal or modification of the concession, or the suspension of the other obligation, in whole or in part
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C03's escape-clause injury standard and its withdrawal, suspension, or modification remedies to periodic review of relief already imposed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Commission shall hold a hearing at which interested parties shall be given reasonable opportunity to be present, to produce evidence, and to be heard
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Tariff Commission shall hold hearings... and shall afford reasonable opportunity for parties interested to be present, to produce evidence, and to be heard at such hearings
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, closely parallel hearing language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Commission may prescribe such rules and regulations for the conduct of investigations under this paragraph as it shall deem appropriate.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The procedure and rules and regulations for such investigations and hearings shall from time to time be prescribed by the Tariff Commission.
shared_material.explanation: Both assign the Commission rulemaking authority over the same investigations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Tariff Commission shall keep under review developments with regard to the product... and shall make periodic reports to the President
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Tariff Commission shall at all times keep informed concerning the operation and effect of provisions relating to duties or other import restrictions... [and] submit to the president... a factual report
shared_material.explanation: The child's periodic-review provision adapts C03's continuing-monitoring and presidential-reporting structure to concessions previously withdrawn, suspended, or modified.
